avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inducer reduces itraconazole levels by up to 50%, decreasing antifungal efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; allow 2 weeks washout before or after itraconazole therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inducer significantly reduces itraconazole plasma concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine; use alternative antifungal if rifampin required

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce CYP3A4, potentially reducing itraconazole bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Limit to dietary amounts; avoid concentrated garlic supplements

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit seed extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: Weak CYP3A4 inhibition may minimally increase itraconazole levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased side effects (edema, headache); consider dose adjustment if high doses used

caution_supplements.name: Milk thistle
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have minor effects on CYP3A4; limited clinical data available
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor clinical response and tolerability

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein blockade increase itraconazole bioavailability, elevating plasma concentrations and risk of toxicity
avoid_foods.action: Completely avoid grapefruit products throughout treatment duration

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May enhance itraconazole absorption and bioavailability; effect varies by formulation (capsules vs. solution)
caution_foods.action: Take itraconazole capsules with food; solution on empty stomach; maintain consistent meal timing

caution_foods.name: Acidic foods/beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Gastric pH affects itraconazole dissolution and absorption (requires acidic environment)
caution_foods.action: Avoid high-dose acid suppressants; no dietary restrictions necessary with normal pH

monitoring_notes: Monitor for signs of itraconazole toxicity (peripheral edema, headache, hypokalemia, elevated transaminases) as CYP3A4 interactions significantly impact drug levels. Assess renal and hepatic function at baseline and periodically during treatment, particularly with concomitant medications or supplements affecting CYP3A4.
